les: Baie mense op een plek, en nie almal gelyk nie
kaps_punt: Mapungubwe: eerste staat in Suider-Afrika 1220 - 1300: Eerste dorp; Duidelike sosiale klasse

items.bewering: In 'n klein nedersetting het die meeste gesinne self hulle kos verbou en hulle diere aangehou.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe (citing Huffman & du Piesanie 2011): life 'centred on family and farming'; Zimbabwe Field Guide, 'Are there cultural links between Mapungubwe and Great Zimbabwe?' (Huffman's settlement pattern): 'commoners live in small homesteads near the agricultural lands'. The 'most families' quantifier is appropriately narrow.

items.bewering: By Mapungubwe het baie meer mense saam op een plek gewoon as in 'n klein nedersetting.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: capital population about 5 000 by 1250; UNESCO nomination material as quoted in search results: an estimated 3 000 to 5 000 people around the hill; southafrica.net: the capital was surrounded by over 200 small villages.

items.bewering: Party van die mense het nie self hulle kos verbou of diere aangehou nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe (Huffman 2005): the leader lived in ritual seclusion on the hilltop with an entourage of soldiers and praise singers, and population growth may have led to full-time pottery specialists; Zimbabwe Field Guide: court officials including a diviner, praise singers and musicians lived on the summit. The lesson says 'party', which does not overstate it.

items.bewering: Een leier het vir die hele dorp en al die mense daar besluit.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'Kingdoms of southern Africa: Mapungubwe': 'The king and his advisors were the decision making body in the state'; Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe (Huffman 2005): sacred leadership with the leader at the top of a tiered hierarchy. The next block adds advisers and people who led on the king's behalf, so the lesson does not imply he ruled entirely alone.

items.bewering: Kos is ook van buite die dorp ingebring. Ander nedersettings het oeste en vee aan die koning gegee.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe (refs. 17, 18): 'A large amount of wealth was accumulated via tributes, which were paid in crops, animals, and sometimes rarer goods'; World History Encyclopedia, Mapungubwe (M. Cartwright, 2019): local chiefs acted as vassals to the king at Mapungubwe.

items.bewering: Mapungubwe was een van die eerste dorpe in Suider-Afrika.
items.blok: Een van die eerste dorpe in Suider-Afrika
items.bron: UCT thesis, The archaeology of Mapela Hill, south-western Zimbabwe: K2 and Mapungubwe are the region's 'presumed first state capitals'; Chirikure et al. 2014, PLOS ONE, 'Zimbabwe Culture before Mapungubwe' (PMC4215987): Mapela Hill, about 90 km north-west, had an elite hilltop occupation earlier. The softened form 'een van die eerste' is correct and should be kept. An unqualified 'die eerste dorp' would now be contested, and the CAPS heading's wording is not repeated in the lesson text.

items.bewering: Van 1220 tot 1300 was die dorp die hoofstad van 'n koninkryk.
items.blok: Een van die eerste dorpe in Suider-Afrika
items.bron: Chirikure et al. 2014, PLOS ONE (PMC4215987): 'the generally accepted dates for the flourishing of Mapungubwe (CE1220–1300)'; South African History Online: Mapungubwe flourished from about 1220 to 1300; Zimbabwe Field Guide: the capital moved from K2 to Mapungubwe Hill around 1220. For the record, these are archaeological estimates. Older literature ends it at about 1290, and Huffman & Woodborne 2021 (South African Journal of Science, AMS dates) put the abandonment at about 1320. The lesson uses the generally accepted span, which is also the CAPS span.

items.bewering: Mapungubwe het in die Limpopo-vallei gelê.
items.blok: Een van die eerste dorpe in Suider-Afrika
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: at the confluence of the Shashe and Limpopo rivers; Huffman & Woodborne 2021, South African Journal of Science: dates from Middle Iron Age sites in the Limpopo Valley, Mapungubwe among them.

items.bewering: Die koning en sy naaste familie het bo-op die Mapungubwe-heuwel gewoon.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: Zimbabwe Field Guide (summarising Huffman): 'from c. 1220 only the ruling elite with their close family occupied its summit', and the leader's young wives had a secluded area there; SAHO: 'The elite lived at the top of Mapungubwe'. Note for accuracy: Huffman places some important male relatives, such as a brother, in prestigious homes below the hill, so 'naaste familie' must not be widened to 'die hele familie'.

items.bewering: Ander mense het namens die koning gelei en hom raad gegee.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: 'a stone-walled residence likely occupied by the principal councillor' (Hrbek); a brother 'would have likely been in charge' of the courts, and the kingdom was divided into a five-tiered hierarchy (Huffman 2005, pp. 34, 50); SAHO: 'The king and his advisors were the decision making body'.

items.bewering: Die gewone mense was boere en beeswagters.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: SAHO: people 'farmed with cattle, sheep and goats', with millet, sorghum and cotton found in storage huts; World History Encyclopedia: cattle herding and growing sorghum and cowpeas; Zimbabwe Field Guide: commoners lived in the valley near the agricultural lands.

items.bewering: Handwerkers onder hulle het potte uit klei gemaak en met yster gewerk.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: SAHO: they 'manufactured their own pottery and metal tools'; World History Encyclopedia: pottery made on a scale suggesting professional potters; Wikipedia (Huffman 2005; Chirikure et al. 2015): men worked iron and most people had iron tools. Wikipedia also says only men of high status worked copper and gold. The lesson names only clay and iron for the commoners, so it is correct as written.

items.bewering: Die mense van die dorp het dus in duidelike sosiale klasse geleef.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: 'one of the first class-based social systems ... in southern Africa' (Wits University); Huffman 2009, Journal of Anthropological Archaeology, as cited in search results: rank at K2 became class distinction at Mapungubwe; Chirikure et al. 2014 accept class distinction at Mapungubwe and dispute only whether it began there.

items.bewering: Waar 'n mens gewoon het. [as a way to see the difference between classes]
items.blok: Waaraan 'n mens die verskil kon sien
items.bron: SAHO: 'location of people's houses separating leaders and commoners'; Zimbabwe Field Guide: the ruler's residence on the summit was built 'to publicise the visibility of hierarchy'.

items.bewering: Hoe 'n mens se woning gebou is. Navorsers verskil oor wat die bouwyse wys.
items.blok: Waaraan 'n mens die verskil kon sien
items.bron: Wikipedia (Huffman 2005; Kim et al. 2015): stone walls demarcated important areas and separated elites from commoners; Zimbabwe Field Guide: the hilltop residence stood on a platform held up by dry-stone walls. That researchers differ is supported by Chirikure et al. 2014 (PMC4215987), who contest Huffman's reading of the walling sequence and note his own uncertainty about 'the status of the Leopards' Kopje walls'. The disclosure is accurate and appropriately brief.

items.bewering: Watter soort voorwerpe 'n mens besit het.
items.blok: Waaraan 'n mens die verskil kon sien
items.bron: SAHO: elite burials on the hilltop held gold and copper ornaments and glass beads, and 'rich and poor ate very different foods'; Wikipedia (Chirikure et al. 2015): poorer farmers used stone and bone tools where most had iron.

items.bewering: Hoe 'n mens begrawe is.
items.blok: Waaraan 'n mens die verskil kon sien
items.bron: SAHO: three people in the hilltop cemetery were buried upright in a sitting position with gold, and 'ordinary men were buried bottom of the hills'; Zimbabwe Field Guide: 23 elite burials, with seated positions reserved for high-status individuals.

items.bewering: Vroeër het mense in die kleiner nedersettings van die vallei meer dieselfde geleef. Hulle huise en besittings het minder verskil as by Mapungubwe.
items.bron: Huffman's model as reported by Wikipedia and the Zimbabwe Field Guide: K2 was a rank-based society, and Indian Ocean trade wealth 'created unprecedented inequalities' that became class distinction at Mapungubwe. The claim is comparative ('meer dieselfde', 'minder verskil'), not a claim of equality, so it holds even though K2 already had some rank and wealth differences, which the Field Guide also describes.

items.bewering: In die dorp kon 'n mens sien dat party mense meer gehad het as ander.
items.bron: SAHO: gold, copper and glass beads in elite hilltop graves, and different diets for rich and poor; Wikipedia: grander homes for important men, and poorer farmers with stone and bone tools.

items.bewering: Sulke klasse was iets nuuts vir die mense van hierdie vallei.
items.bron: Huffman, quoted by the Zimbabwe Field Guide and the Mail & Guardian (15 June 1995): Mapungubwe gives 'the earliest evidence for class distinction and sacred leadership in southern Africa', and royalty were set apart from the populace for the first time. The main challenge, Mapela Hill (Chirikure et al. 2014), is about 90 km away and, by the UCT thesis abstract, 'located outside the Middle Limpopo'. So narrowing the claim to 'hierdie vallei' keeps it inside the supported reading, and it must not be widened to 'Suider-Afrika'.

items.bewering: Niemand in die dorp het neergeskryf hoe die mense daar geleef het nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: knowledge of society rests on the remains of buildings, because 'the Mapungubwean people left no written record'; University of Pretoria Mapungubwe Archive: the record is archaeological, from UP's excavations since 1933.

items.bewering: Argeoloë het bo-op en onderaan die heuwel in die grond gegrawe. Hulle het gekyk waar voorwerpe gelê het.
items.bron: University of Pretoria repository: Fouché's report on excavations at Mapungubwe (1933–1935), and Gardner's six seasons at K2 and on Mapungubwe Hill (1935–1940); SAHO: graves both on top of the hill and at its foot; UNESCO nomination as quoted in search results: commoners on the southern terrace at the foot of the hill.

items.bewering: Bo-op die heuwel het hulle ander soorte voorwerpe gevind as onderaan. So kon hulle aflei dat mense van 'n hoër klas bo gewoon het.
items.bron: SAHO and the Zimbabwe Field Guide: gold objects, among them the golden rhinoceros, and elite burials on the hilltop; Wikipedia (Hrbek): 'Gold objects were uncovered in elite burials on the royal hill'. The inference from high place to high class is the one archaeologists draw (Huffman, via the Mail & Guardian 1995 and the Zimbabwe Field Guide). The step from position to class is presented as an inference ('kon hulle aflei'), which is correct.

items.bewering: In die grafte kon hulle sien dat nie almal op dieselfde manier begrawe is nie.
items.bron: SAHO: three seated burials with gold and copper ornaments and glass beads on the hilltop, and ordinary people buried lower down; Wikipedia: most people buried with few or no accessories, three different; men buried in kraals and women outside them (Chirikure et al. 2015).

items.bewering: dorp: 'n Groot nedersetting waar nie almal self hulle kos verbou of diere aanhou nie.
items.bron: Susan Reynolds' 1977 definition of a town, widely used by historians and archaeologists (via Cambridge, 'Towns and their hinterlands'): a permanent, concentrated settlement whose people do not live mainly by farming and get food from elsewhere; V. Gordon Childe's urban model: larger than earlier villages, with specialists who do not produce food. 'Nie almal' is the correctly narrow form.

items.bewering: sosiale klas: 'n Groep mense met dieselfde plek in die samelewing. Sulke groepe staan bo en onder mekaar en nie net langs mekaar nie.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary entries for upper, middle and lower class: classes are defined by their position above and below one another, by status. Checking the spatial image for its mapping: 'bo en onder' maps rank onto height. That holds, and it fits this lesson, where the higher class literally lived higher up. A learner reasoning further might expect every hilltop dweller to be upper class everywhere, but the lesson presents height only as evidence at Mapungubwe, so the mapping does not mislead.

items.bewering: nedersetting: 'n Nedersetting is 'n plek waar 'n groep mense saam woon.
items.bron: Consistent with the standard sense of 'settlement' used in the same Reynolds/Childe literature (Cambridge; Wikipedia, History of cities): a place where people live permanently in a group. Simple and not false.

items.bewering: handwerker: Iemand wat met eie hande dinge maak, soos potte of ystergereedskap.
items.bron: Standard sense of craftsperson. Both examples are attested crafts at Mapungubwe (SAHO: pottery and metal tools; Wikipedia: men worked iron).

items.bewering: argeoloog: 'n Argeoloog ondersoek die dinge wat mense lank gelede gemaak, gebruik en agtergelaat het om te leer hoe hulle geleef het, en grawe is een van die maniere om daardie dinge te vind.
items.bron: Britannica, 'archaeology': 'the scientific study of the material remains of past human life and activities'. Britannica's summary lists locating and mapping sites, excavating, and then classifying, dating and interpreting finds, so 'grawe is een van die maniere' is the accurate form.

opsomming: Every claim holds, and the lesson's careful forms must be kept as they are: 'een van die eerste dorpe', 'iets nuuts vir die mense van hierdie vallei' (Mapela Hill outside the Middle Limpopo may predate Mapungubwe, so neither may be widened to all of southern Africa), and 'naaste familie'. The dates 1220 to 1300 are the generally accepted span, although a 2021 dating study puts the end nearer 1320.
